newsitem.title: USA: Colombia 1998 growth seen at 5-5.5 pct - official.
newsitem.headline: Colombia 1998 growth seen at 5-5.5 pct - official.

text.p: An expected increase in private investment in manufacturing and other sectors of the Colombian economy will fuel solid growth of 5.0 to 5.5 percent in 1998, said Clemente del Valle, director general of Public Credit in Colombia.

"There will be a strong recuperation of private investment in manufacturing and other sectors because of a lower interest rate policy, which is currently undergoing," del Valle told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said the 5.0 to 5.5 percent growth would also be fueled by investments in the country's infrastructure.
"We have very important investments in the infrastructure side during this year and the following year, which will be also fueling the growth," del Valle said.
Del Valle said expected economic growth in 1997 of around 4.0 to 4.5 percent would, in part, come from the oil sector.
In regard to the nationwide strike, which is now in its third day, del Valle said he believed people were starting to understand the need for fiscal discipline.

"They (labor unions) are trying to get a strong reaction. However, I think...everybody understands that we have to be tight and currently they are sitting down negotiating trying to get closer in terms of what the government can do and what the trade unions obviously want" to do, del Valle said.
"But I think people are starting to understand that the government is serious on its need to establish a very tight budget for this year."

Earlier today, union leaders resumed talks with government ministers in Bogota to end the strike with public sector workers, but no progress was reported when the talks adjourned for two hours shortly before 1200 EST.

Public sector workers are calling for a 21.5 percent wage rise and an end to planned privatization of regional and national industries, but the government has so far stuck to its offer of a weighted 13.5 percent pay increase and has refused to budge on privatization plans.

"As I mentioned, it is something normal when you are establishing a very tight increase in wages for the public servants. It is understandable that there has been a reaction at the trade union level," del Valle added.
